He preferred the view of al-Harfi that "they know" is a resumptive (isti'naf) sentence in meaning. The discussion of the Exalted Lord's words:

﴿And they will have no intercessors among their associates, and they will disbelieve in their associates.﴾ That is, they will not have anyone to protect them from the punishment of Allah, as they used to claim. ﴿And they will disbelieve in their associates﴾ means that they will deny their divinity and their being partners with Allah, once they come to know the reality of their situation. ﴿On the Day the Hour is established, on that day they will be separated﴾ [al-Rum: 14]. That is, the believers and the disbelievers will be distinguished from one another in their places and their conditions. ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a meadow, made joyful﴾ [al-Rum: 15]. That is, they will not be absent from it, and it will not be lightened for them. ﴿So exalted is Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ [al-Rum: 17]. ﴿And to Him is praise in the heavens and the earth, and at night and when you dhuhr [i.e., at midday]﴾ [al-Rum: 18].

Al-Mahayimi said: i.e., by prayer, from the death of the heart to its life, and from the life of the soul to its death. And He revives its land with the growth of virtuous states, after its death through base states, and vice versa through abandoning them. Glory be to Him who created them, set them in motion, and turned them to the various kinds of livelihood, and differentiated among them in knowledge and understanding, in beauty and ugliness, in wealth and poverty, and in happiness and misery.

[ (p-4773) ] ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the diversity of your languages and your colors. Abu al-Su'ud said: The expression of it by "command" serves to indicate the perfection of power and independence from beginnings and causes. The intended meaning of their "standing" is not their creation, because that was already described by His saying: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾; nor is their standing without a visible supporter, as has been said, for that belongs to the completions of their creation, even though it is not stated explicitly, relying on what was mentioned in other places in His saying: ﴿He created the heavens without pillars that you can see﴾ [Luqman: 10], and so on. Rather, their standing and their continuance in the state they are in, until their appointed term, is what His saying before this expresses: ﴿Allah did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth and for an appointed term﴾ [Ar-Rum: 8]. Since this verse comes after the rest of the enumerated signs and is connected to the resurrection in existence, it was placed after them and also connected to it in the mention. Thus He said: ﴿Then, when He calls you with one call from the earth, behold, you will come out﴾ [Ar-Rum: 25]. This is a statement brought to inform of the occurrence and existence of the resurrection, after the end of the term of their standing, (p-4774) and it is consequent upon the enumeration of His signs that indicate it, not included in their series as has been said. It is as if it were said: And among His signs is the standing of the heavens and the earth in their forms by His command, until an appointed term that Allah has determined for their standing; then, when He calls you from the earth, after the end of the term, while you are in your graves, with one call, by saying: "O dead! Come out!", you will suddenly be coming out of it. This is His saying: ﴿On that Day they will follow the caller﴾ [Ta-Ha: 108]. End.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[26–27] ﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him.﴾ ﴿And it is He who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him. To Him belongs the highest description in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ [al-Rum: 27].

(p-4775) ﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, by creation, ownership and disposal. ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾, that is, submitting to His disposal, not refusing it. ﴿And it is He who originates creation, then repeats it﴾ [al-Rum: 27], that is, after their death. Abu al-Su'ud said: its repetition is for the sake of further affirmation and as a preparation for what follows it in His words, exalted is He, ﴿and that is easier for Him﴾ [al-Rum: 27], that is, than the beginning; that is, in relation to what the reasoning of the addressees requires, for whoever among them repeats the making of a thing finds it easier and less difficult than originating it. Otherwise, both are equal for Him, glorified is He, in ease.

Subtleties:

The first: the pronoun is masculine (yu'iduhu) although it refers back to the repetition (al-i'adah), because the repetition is interpreted as "that He repeat (an yu'ida)."

The second: al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, why is the complement (al-silah) delayed in His words ﴿and that is easier for Him﴾ [al-Rum: 27] while it was placed first in His words ﴿It is easy for Me﴾ [Maryam: 9]? I say: there the purpose is restriction (qasd al-ikhtisas), and that is its core point. It was said, "It is easy for Me," although it seems difficult to you that one should be born between an old man and a barren woman. But here, there is no sense in restriction, how so? The matter is based on what they understand, namely that repetition is easier than beginning. Had the complement been placed first, the meaning would have changed.

Al-Nasir said: This is a precious statement, deserving to be written with melted gold rather than ink, and restriction is only conveyed by placing before what ought to be placed after.

The third: al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, why was repetition deemed great in His words ﴿Then when He calls you out of the earth﴾ [al-Rum: 25], until it seems to be preferred over the standing of the heavens and the earth by His command, and then it was made light afterward? I say: repetition in itself is great, but it was made light by comparison with origination. End.

Al-Nasir said: The question only raises the greatness of repetition from its being conjoined with "then" (thumma), signalling the difference of its rank and the loftiness of its status. His statement in the answer, that it was made light in relation to origination, does not hold. For repetition is mentioned here right after the standing of the heavens and the earth by His command, and their standing, as origination and creation, is greater than repetition; thus repetition is made great in relation to what is conjoined to it, namely origination, and the difficulty returns. The resolution, and God knows best, is that "thumma" is taken in its own sense, indicating the lapse of time and not the lapse of ranks. And if it is granted that it indicates the lapse of ranks, then it is on the basis that the rank of the conjoined-to is the higher and the rank of the conjoined is the lower, and that is rare in its use for the lapse of ranks, for the conjoined in such cases is in most instances higher in rank than the conjoined-to. End.

In the marginal notes of al-Qadi: "thumma" is either for the lapse of time of the conjoined, so it stays in its literal sense, or it is for the greatness of what the conjoined contains, the reviving of the dead, so it signifies difference in rank and not temporal lapse. The intended greatness is greatness in itself and in relation to the conjoined-to. So it does not contradict His words ﴿and that is easier for Him﴾ [al-Rum: 27], nor its being greater than the standing of the heavens and the earth, because it is the aim of bringing into being and creation, and by it the happy and the wretched are established in the ranks and the abysses, and it is the purpose of creating the earth and the heavens. So there is no impossibility in what he prohibited, and this is a precious benefit. It is also permissible to take it as general distance, encompassing both temporal and rank-based distance, as in the Sharh al-Kashshaf.

(p-4777) The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[28–29] ﴿He has coined for you a parable from yourselves: Do you have among those whom your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided you, so that you are equal therein, and you fear them as you fear one another among yourselves? Thus do We detail the signs for a people who reason.﴾ ﴿Rather, those who wronged followed their own desires without knowledge. So who can guide one whom Allah has sent astray? For them there are no helpers.﴾ [al-Rum: 29]

﴿He has coined for you a parable﴾, i.e., by which the falsity of association (shirk) becomes clear. ﴿From yourselves﴾, i.e., drawn from their own circumstances, which are the closest matters to you and the most evident in disclosure. ﴿Do you have among those whom your right hands possess﴾, i.e., among the slaves and bondwomen: ﴿any partners in what We have provided you﴾, i.e., of wealth and other things: ﴿so that you are equal therein﴾, i.e., you are equal in disposing of what has been mentioned without any distinction. ﴿And you fear them﴾, i.e., you dread that you would act independently in disposing of it without their opinion, and this is another predicate of "you" (antum): ﴿as you fear one another among yourselves﴾, i.e., as some of you fear others among the free men who share with you in what has been mentioned. The meaning is the negation of the content of what was detailed in the interrogative sentence; that is, you do not accept that your possessions, which are lent to you, your mamluks, who are like you in humanity and are not created by you but belong to Allah Exalted, should share with you in what is yours. How then do you associate with Him, glorified is He, in worship, which is among His essential attributes, His creation, indeed the product of His creation, since you fashion it with your own hands and then worship it? This is conveyed by Abu al-Su'ud. ﴿Thus do We detail the signs﴾, i.e., in a manner like this clear detailing, the signs are made plain: ﴿for a people who reason.﴾ ﴿Rather, those who wronged followed their own desires without knowledge﴾ [al-Rum: 29], i.e., without certainty and proof: ﴿So who can guide one whom Allah has sent astray?﴾ [al-Rum: 29], i.e., the cause of diverting his choice toward his own acquisition; that is, no one is able to guide him. ﴿For them there are no helpers﴾ [al-Rum: 29], i.e., who could help them against Allah if He intends punishment for them.

Thus do We detail the signs for a people who reason.﴾ ﴿Rather, those who wronged followed their own desires without knowledge. So who can guide one whom Allah has sent astray? For them there are no helpers.﴾ [al-Rum: 29]

﴿He has coined for you a parable﴾, i.e., by which the falsity of association (shirk) becomes clear. ﴿From yourselves﴾, i.e., drawn from their own circumstances, which are the closest matters to you and the most evident in disclosure. ﴿Do you have among those whom your right hands possess﴾, i.e., among the slaves and bondwomen: ﴿any partners in what We have provided you﴾, i.e., of wealth and other things: ﴿so that you are equal therein﴾, i.e., you are equal in disposing of what has been mentioned without any distinction. ﴿And you fear them﴾, i.e., you dread that you would act independently in disposing of it without their opinion, and this is another predicate of "you" (antum): ﴿as you fear one another among yourselves﴾, i.e., as some of you fear others among the free men who share with you in what has been mentioned. The meaning is the negation of the content of what was detailed in the interrogative sentence; that is, you do not accept that your possessions, which are lent to you, your mamluks, who are like you in humanity and are not created by you but belong to Allah Exalted, should share with you in what is yours. How then do you associate with Him, glorified is He, in worship, which is among His essential attributes, His creation, indeed the product of His creation, since you fashion it with your own hands and then worship it? This is conveyed by Abu al-Su'ud. ﴿Thus do We detail the signs﴾, i.e., in a manner like this clear detailing, the signs are made plain: ﴿for a people who reason.﴾ ﴿Rather, those who wronged followed their own desires without knowledge﴾ [al-Rum: 29], i.e., without certainty and proof: ﴿So who can guide one whom Allah has sent astray?﴾ [al-Rum: 29], i.e., the cause of diverting his choice toward his own acquisition; that is, no one is able to guide him. ﴿For them there are no helpers﴾ [al-Rum: 29], i.e., who could help them against Allah if He intends punishment for them.

(p-4778) The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[30–32] ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, the fitrah of Allah upon which He created mankind. There is no alteration to the creation of Allah. That is the upright religion, but most of mankind do not know.﴾ ﴿Turning back in repentance to Him and fear Him, and establish prayer, and do not be among those who associate partners with Allah,﴾ ﴿of those who divided their religion and became sects, each faction rejoicing in what it has.﴾ [al-Rum: 30–32]

﴿So set your face toward the religion﴾ means: straighten it for Him, make it upright, and turn toward it. In the noble wording there is an *isti'arah tamthiliyyah* (metaphorical allegory, a figure in which an entire scene is depicted), by likening the one commanded to hold fast to the religion, to observe its rights, not to transgress its limits, and to attend to its affairs, to one who is ordered to look at a matter, fix his gaze upon it, direct his sight and turn his face toward it, in order to watch over it and to attend to its preservation. ﴿Inclining to truth﴾ means: turning away from everything other than Him toward Him.

Al-Mahayimi said: Returning to Him is not difficult, because ﴿the fitrah of Allah upon which He created mankind﴾, meaning that the intellect of every individual indicates that the world is originated and requires an originator, and there is no indication at all that it requires a plurality. Therefore, the claim of plurality is a change to the fitrah. But ﴿there is no alteration to the creation of Allah﴾, meaning there is no change to the faculty of intellect that Allah created for reasoning. ﴿That﴾ refers either to the religion commanded to be faced toward, or to the fitrah. ﴿The upright religion﴾ means the straight one in which there is no crookedness. Al-Mahayimi said: Even if no proof stands with those who alter it to show the impossibility of plurality, this is what the fitrah demands. ﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾ means: that this is what the fitrah demands. The fitrah is the most decisive and conclusive refutation of the disputant's noise, because it is among the matters that do not fall under acquisition and choice.

As for His saying, ﴿Turning back in repentance to Him﴾ [al-Rum: 31], it means returning to Him in repentance and penitence: ﴿And who forgives sins except Allah?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 135]. This is a circumstantial clause (*hal*) from the subject of the verb "ilzamu" (adhere), which is implied as governing "fitrah," or from the subject of "aqim" (establish) according to the sense, since it is not meant for one specific individual; or because the address is to him (ﷺ) and to his community; or on the basis that the coordinated element has been omitted, meaning: establish, you and your community, and the circumstantial clause applies to all of them: ﴿and fear Him, and establish prayer, and do not be among those who associate partners with Allah﴾ [al-Rum: 31]. ﴿Of those who divided their religion﴾ [al-Rum: 32] means they made it into differing religions according to the divergence of their desires. ﴿And became sects﴾ [al-Rum: 32] means factions. ﴿Each faction rejoicing in what it has﴾ [al-Rum: 32] means each faction among them rejoices in its own school, delighted, considering its falsehood to be truth.

Al-Qashani said: He means those who depart from the true religion, scattering into different sects, each faction, when the fitrah is clouded and the veils thicken, rejoices in what its readiness demands of veils, because that is the requirement of the nature of its veil. Thus its state corresponds to the accidental readiness, even if it does not suit the reality according to the innate readiness. For this reason, punishment becomes necessary through it when the accident passes away.

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[33–36] ﴿When harm touches people, they call upon their Lord, turning to Him in repentance. Then when He lets them taste mercy from Him, behold, a group of them associate others with their Lord.﴾ ﴿So that they may deny what We have given them. Enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.﴾ [al-Rum: 34] ﴿Or have We sent down upon them an authority which speaks of what they used to associate with Him?﴾ [al-Rum: 35] ﴿And when We let people taste mercy, they rejoice in it; but if an evil befalls them because of what their hands have sent forward, behold, they despair.﴾ [al-Rum: 36]

﴿When harm touches people﴾, i.e., hardship. ﴿they call upon their Lord, turning to Him in repentance﴾, i.e., returning to Him alone, apart from their partners. ﴿Then when He lets them taste mercy from Him﴾, i.e., deliverance from that hardship. ﴿behold, a group of them associate others with their Lord.﴾ ﴿So that they may deny what We have given them﴾ [al-Rum: 34], i.e., by means of the very thing for the sake of which We gave them mercy, which is turning in repentance. The lam here is lam al-'aqibah (the lam of consequence, indicating outcome). It has also been said that it is the lam of threat (lam al-amr al-tahdidi), like His saying: ﴿Enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know﴾, i.e., the consequence of your enjoyment and its ruin.

﴿Or have We sent down upon them an authority﴾ [al-Rum: 35], i.e., a clear, overpowering proof. ﴿which speaks﴾ [al-Rum: 35], i.e., speaks by way of indication, as in His saying: ﴿This Our Book speaks against you with truth﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 29]. ﴿of what they used to associate with Him﴾ [al-Rum: 35], i.e., of their associating others. This is a rhetorical question of denial, meaning that nothing of that sort has occurred.

﴿And when We let people taste mercy﴾ [al-Rum: 36], i.e., a blessing of health and abundance. ﴿they rejoice in it﴾ [al-Rum: 36], i.e., in insolence and boasting, not in praise and gratitude. ﴿But if an evil befalls them﴾ [al-Rum: 36], i.e., hardship, ﴿because of what their hands have sent forward﴾ [al-Rum: 36], i.e., of sins and wrongdoings, ﴿behold, they despair﴾ [al-Rum: 36], i.e., they lose hope in the mercy of Allah.

He said: This is a denunciation of man as such, except for those whom Allah protects and enables. When a blessing touches man, he becomes insolent, and He said: ﴿The evils have gone away from me, surely he is exultant and boastful﴾ [Hud: 10], i.e., he rejoices within himself and boasts over others. When hardship touches him, he despairs and gives up hope that any good will come to him at all after that. Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Except those who are patient and do righteous deeds﴾ [Hud: 11], i.e., they are patient in adversity and do righteous deeds in ease, as is established in the Sahih: "How wondrous is the affair of the believer! Allah does not decree for him any decree except that it is good for him. If prosperity reaches him, he gives thanks, and that is good for him; and if adversity reaches him, he is patient, and that is good for him."

[37] ﴿Have they not seen that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾

﴿Have they not seen that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ Al-Zamakhshari said: He rebukes them, since they know that He is the One who extends and restricts. When He, exalted is He, had explained that the evil had befallen them because of what their hands had earned, He followed it with mention of what must be done and what must be avoided, in His words:

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 30, verses 38–39:

Discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[38–39] ﴿So give to the near of kin his due, and to the needy and the wayfarer. That is best for those who desire the Countenance of Allah, and they are the successful.﴾ ﴿And that which you give in interest (riba) to increase the wealth of people does not increase in the sight of Allah; but that which you give in zakah, desiring the Countenance of Allah — it is those who will have their reward multiplied.﴾ [al-Rum: 39]

﴿So give to the near of kin his due﴾ means: of righteousness and kinship ties. Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, used this verse as evidence for the obligation of maintenance for those within the prohibited degrees (mahram) when they are needy and unable to earn a living, because (ati) is an imperative indicating obligation. What is apparent from (al-haqq), by the context of what precedes it, is that it refers to one's wealth, and this is a sound inference. ﴿And the needy﴾ refers to one who has nothing with which to support himself, or who has something that does not suffice for his sufficiency. ﴿And the wayfarer﴾ means the traveler who asks for help in it and the one who has been cut off from his journey. First: This verse resembles the verse: ﴿Allah destroys riba and makes charity grow﴾ [al-Baqarah: 276], and that concerns the riba of sale, which was widespread among the people of Makkah until it became a firmly established habit among them, by which they drained the wealth of many of the poor, which went beyond the limits of mercy, compassion, and human perfection. Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 30, verse 40:

The discussion of His, the Exalted's, saying:

[40] ﴿Allah is the One who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will bring you to life. Is there any of your partners who does anything of that? Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾

Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ Al-Qadi said: He, the Exalted, affirmed for Himself the necessary attributes of divinity (lawazim al-uluhiyyah), and absolutely negated them from what they took as partners to Him, such as idols and others, emphasizing with a rejection (inkar) based on what proof (burhan) and direct observation (i'an) indicate, and on which there is consensus (wifaq). Then it was deduced from that His holiness (taqaddus) above having any partners. End.

**The explanation of His words, the Exalted:**

[41–43] ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned, so that He may let them taste some of what they have done, that perhaps they may return.﴾ ﴿Say, "Travel through the earth and see what was the end of those before you; most of them were polytheists."﴾ [Ar-Rum: 42] ﴿So set your face toward the upright religion before there comes a Day which no repelling will avert from Allah. That Day they will be separated.﴾ [Ar-Rum: 43]

﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea﴾ means: the abundance of harms and acts of disobedience on the surface of the earth and on the decks of ships in the depths of the sea. ﴿Because of what the hands of people have earned﴾ means: because of sins and ruinous deeds. Thus corruption spread widely, its contagion proliferated, and it was inherited from generation to generation wherever they settled and wherever they travelled. ﴿So that He may let them taste some of what they have done, that perhaps they may return.﴾ The *lam* (the particle lam) here indicates consequence (*lil-'aqibah*), meaning: the appearance of evils is due to them, which made it necessary that Allah let them taste the evil consequences of their deeds, in the hope that they would return. It was also said that the *lam* indicates purpose (*lil-'illah*), in the sense that the appearance of drought, famine and drowning is due to the ill omen of their acts of disobedience, so that He may let them taste the evil of some of their deeds in this world, before He punishes them with all of them in the Hereafter, that perhaps they may turn back from what they are upon. This is like His words, the Exalted: ﴿And whatever misfortune strikes you is because of what your hands have earned﴾ [Ash-Shura: 30].

﴿Say, "Travel through the earth and see what was the end of those before you; most of them were polytheists."﴾ [Ar-Rum: 42] meaning: so Allah, glorified is He, made them taste the evil of their end, because of their polytheism, which entails every sin and disobedience. ﴿So set your face toward the upright religion before there comes a Day which no repelling will avert﴾ [Ar-Rum: 43] meaning: no one is able to turn it back. His words ﴿from Allah﴾ [Ar-Rum: 43] are connected either to "comes" or to "repelling," because the latter is a verbal noun with the sense of "none will repel it, Exalted is He," since His will is tied to its coming. In this there is an exclusion of anyone else's repelling, by way of a demonstrative argument. It was objected: if this is so, then it would require that the word be nunated (tanwin) because it resembles a noun with a genitive attached. It was answered that what resembles the attached noun may be treated, in omitting its tanwin, as in the hadith: "There is no preventer of what You have given."

﴿That Day they will be separated﴾ [Ar-Rum: 43] means: they will scatter like scattered moths, or one group will be in Paradise and another group in the Blazing Fire, like His words: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, that Day they will be divided﴾ [Ar-Rum: 14].

**The commentary on His words (Exalted is He):**

[54–55] ﴿It is God who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the Knowing, the Powerful.﴾ ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear that they had not remained but an hour. Thus were they deluded.﴾ [al-Rum: 55]

﴿It is God who created you from weakness﴾ It is read with a fatha and with a damma on the ḍād (ضَعْف / ضُعْف). That is: from a weak origin, which is the drop of semen (nutfah). ﴿Then made after weakness﴾ means the state of childhood and youth. ﴿Strength﴾ means the state of puberty and vigor, up to the age of maturity (al-ikhtihāl, the middle years) and the attainment of full maturity (bulūgh al-ashudd). ﴿Then made after strength weakness and gray hair﴾ means with old age and decrepitude. ﴿He creates what He wills﴾ means from among things, and among them are these stages through which a human being passes. ﴿And He is the Knowing, the Powerful﴾ means the One whose knowledge and power are vast. How so? This alternation through different states, and the change from one attribute to another, is the clearest proof of the knowledge and power of the Maker, may He be glorified, which entails that He alone is deserving of divinity.

﴿On the Day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear that they had not remained but an hour﴾ [al-Rum: 55] means in the world or in the graves. They estimate the length of their stay in this way only out of belittling it. Or they forget, or they lie, or they guess.

﴿Thus were they deluded﴾ [al-Rum: 55] means in the same manner they were turned away from truth and verification in the world. Likewise, they used to decide their affairs contrary to the truth. This is in al-Kashshāf.

Ibn Kathir said: He, Exalted, informs about the ignorance of the disbelievers in this world and the Hereafter. In this world they did what they did, such as worshipping idols. In the Hereafter, there will also be great ignorance from them. Among it is their swearing by God that they had not remained but a single hour in the world. Their aim by this is that the proof would not be established against them, and that they were not given respite so that an excuse could be accepted from them. End.

Al-Shihāb said: What is meant by His words ﴿Thus were they deluded﴾ [al-Rum: 55] is the similarity of their two states in lying and in not returning to what knowledge requires, because the basis of their affair is ignorance and falsehood. The purpose of citing the verse is to describe the criminals by their persistence in falsehood and in the lie to which they had become accustomed. End.

It has also been said: their oath was an independent one, for the sake of the world, when they witnessed the Hereafter, out of regret for what they had squandered in the world.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 30, verses 56–57:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[56–57] ﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say, "You have indeed remained, according to the Decree of Allah, until the Day of Resurrection. So this is the Day of Resurrection, but you were not aware."﴾ ﴿So on that Day, those who did wrong will not benefit from their excuse, nor will they be asked to make amends.﴾ [al-Rum: 57].

﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith﴾: as a refutation of what they swore to, and to inform them of the reality. ﴿"You have indeed remained in the Book of Allah"﴾, i.e., in what Allah has decreed and made obligatory by His wisdom, ﴿"until the Day of Resurrection. So this is the Day of Resurrection, but you were not aware"﴾, i.e., that it is true, because of your neglect in seeking the truth and following it. ﴿"So on that Day, those who did wrong will not benefit"﴾ [al-Rum: 57], i.e., by associating partners with Allah, or denying His lordship, or His messengership, or anything whose belief is obligatory: ﴿"their excuse"﴾ [al-Rum: 57], i.e., [their claim] that they disbelieved out of ignorance, since it was only due to their negligence in removing it, or out of obstinacy. ﴿"Nor will they be asked to make amends"﴾ [al-Rum: 57], i.e., they will not be asked to seek reconciliation (i'tab), that is, the removal of displeasure (al-'atab) through repentance and obedience. For these two, although they erase disbelief and sins, they had that effect only during the life of this world, and not otherwise.
